name: Postcard Post
character: Sky blue and a postage scale: quilted postcards that actually go in the mail, cancelled and all.

sections.title: {{guild_name}}
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: {{guild_name}} makes postcards you can mail. We meet {{meeting_info}} with a scale, a stamp box, and a list of addresses that want cloth.

sections.heading: Mail night
sections.note: USPS size is 4 by 6, stiff enough to survive a canceling machine. If it is floppy, add a cardstock middle. If it is too thick, it is a parcel.

items.title: The swap
items.body: Each month you mail one and receive one. Addresses drawn from a hat.

items.title: The public ones
items.body: A stack by the library desk. Anyone may take a postcard if they will write a real note on the back.

items.title: The show
items.body: Once a year we pin the returned cards to a map before they go home in albums.

sections.title: Bring stamps
sections.body: Dues cover the room and the library stack. Postage is yours.

sections.title: About {{guild_name}}
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: A guild that treats the mail as a gallery.

sections.heading: How we started
sections.html: Sample text — replace me: Paper postcards vanish. Cloth ones get kept on fridges. {{guild_name}} started as a dare to see if the post office would cancel a quilted square. They will, if you stay inside the size and the thickness.

items.title: Monthly swap
items.body: Twelve cards out, twelve back, if the mail behaves.

items.title: April map
items.body: We pin every returned card on a wall map of the country.

items.title: December thick
items.body: Holiday cards may be a hair thicker. We still weigh them.

sections.title: How to Mail Cloth
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Size, stiffness, stamps, and what happens when a card comes back crumpled.

items.title: Size
items.body: 4 by 6 inches. Corners may be round. A hanging sleeve is how you get it returned as a parcel.

items.title: Middle
items.body: Cardstock or a thin plastic. Quilted cloth alone will crumple in the machine.

items.title: Address
items.body: Ink on a fabric label, or a paper label stitched on. Pencil disappears.

items.a: No. That is the point of a postcard. If it vanishes, sew another.
A few of us do. Extra stamps, extra time, a customs form that confuses everyone.

sections.title: Membership
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: You need twelve addresses in you, including strangers.

items.q: I do not want strangers to have my home address.
items.a: Use a PO box or the guild's mailbox. We will not publish a roster to the public pile.

items.q: Can it be art quilt tiny work, not cute?
items.a: Please. Cute is allowed. Cute is not required.
